title: 4-to-1 Multiplexer
constraints: Purely combinational: no clock and no registers.
`y` must follow any input change immediately (checked 1 ns after `sel` changes).
Must be synthesizable and must not infer latches.
hints: A `case` on `sel` inside `always @(*)` / `always_comb` — or `with sel select` in VHDL — maps directly onto a multiplexer.
Latches appear when `y` is not assigned for some value of `sel`. Cover every case, or add a `default` / `when others` branch.
A one-line alternative: nested conditional operators on `sel[1]` and `sel[0]`.

examples.title: sel = 0
examples.input:
a = 0x11, b = 0x22, c = 0x33, d = 0x44, sel = 0
(+ 64 random vectors)

examples.title: sel = 2
examples.input:
a = 0x11, b = 0x22, c = 0x33, d = 0x44, sel = 2
(+ 64 random vectors)

examples.title: only sel changes
examples.input:
a..d fixed at 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44
sel = 0 → 1 → 2 → 3, one step per ns
